svg.font-family: -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'SF Pro Text', 'Helvetica Neue', Arial, sans-serif
svg.title: Component · Gallery filmstrip · preview
svg.desc: Mirrors GalleryFilmstrip in App/GalleryItemView.swift (macOS, 2026-09-13) — the grid folded into one row under the Gallery's item view: every project the sidebar, the search and the sort leave in the grid, in the grid's order, as 80×60 ProjectThumbnailView tiles (4:3, cornerRadius 6) 8 pt apart in a LazyHStack padded 16 at the sides and 12 above and below, inside a horizontal ScrollView with no indicators; the focused project carries the grid's own 2.5 pt LL.accent ring and is kept centred (ScrollViewReader, anchor .center, 0.25 s easeInOut on a change); a click on any other tile asks the host to move there (GalleryView.move(to:)), ← → step through the same order, and the header trailing reads "n of N". Full window width, on LL.cardBackground — under the inspector and the rail alike, the Lightroom / Photos convention, and the one place a strip can go without either editor knowing about it. Drawn here as measured on the Debug build at 1310×800 (2026-09-13): the strip is 92 pt from its divider to the tab bar's safe-area clearance — tiles at y 12–72 — although its frame is 84; the white background then continues under the 58 pt clearance to the window edge (a SwiftUI .background ignores the safe-area inset), which the screen files draw. This file's fourteen tiles are the gallery mirrors' own tile art in the grid's order (gallery.svg t1…t12 and two more), so the strip reads as the same library the grid shows. One file per focused position — see components/README.md. **2026-09-26 — the holdings pill on every tile** (connected asset states, plan §12 and §16; GalleryFilmstrip.tile in App/GalleryItemView.swift: HoldingsPill(captureID:) in an .overlay(alignment: .bottomTrailing) with .scaleEffect(0.8, anchor: .bottomTrailing).padding(3), under the focus ring's own overlay): each tile wears the grid tile's pill at 0.8, its bottom-right corner 3 pt in — a pill W wide sits at x = tileMaxX − 3 − 0.8W, y 54.6–69 (72 − 3 − 14.4). The states are the fourteen projects gallery.svg's grid draws, in the grid's order: 1 both.safe (River Sunset to Dusk — the photos and its three blends here, all backed up), 2 here.uploading, 3 here.needs, 4 both.needs, 5 here.safe, 6 here.needs, 7 there.blend-here.safe (the originals removed here, the blends kept), 8 there.safe (a preview: the tick stays), 9 here.safe, 10 here.safe, 11 here.needs, 12 here.safe, 13 here.safe, 14 nowhere.originals (the originals nowhere reachable). THE PILLS ARE INLINED, NOT REFERENCED: each <g data-component="holdings-pill.<state>.svg"> is that generated file's markup verbatim (its mask ids suffixed with the tile) scaled 0.8, because a component referenced from inside a component is not followed once a screen places the strip — tested 2026-09-26 with Quick Look: a pill <image> in this file draws when the file is opened alone and vanishes from gallery.item*.svg — and components/README.md's rule is flat files, never nested. They are copies: re-copy them from holdings-pill.make.py's output whenever the pill changes. **THIS FILE (2026-09-26): focus on tile 8** — gallery.svg's there.safe interval, a preview whose originals are on PicPlace — for the item view on the editor's preview page (macOS/gallery.item.preview*.svg). The fourteen tiles span 16–1240 of the 1310 pt strip, so the horizontal ScrollView has nothing to scroll: its content sits at the leading edge and GalleryFilmstrip's scrollTo(focusedID, anchor: .center) cannot move it — only the ring moves (x 633.25, the 2.5 pt strokeBorder 1.25 in). A copy of gallery-filmstrip.interval.svg but for the ring, the title and data-state.

g.data-symbol: camera.fill + a slash knocked through (no SF camera.slash)
